name: AlphaQ: Calibration-Free Bit Allocation for Mixture-of-Experts Quantization
problem: Mixed-precision MoE quantization allocates bit widths from a calibration set, but for frontier MoE models the training data is proprietary so the calibration set is an imperfect surrogate and mis-ranks expert importance.
mechanism: Drops calibration entirely. Uses Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization (HT-SR) theory - the empirical law that the quality of a subnetwork is predictable from the heavy-tailed structure of its weight spectrum without any data - to assign bit widths per expert from the weight spectrum alone, grounded in the large cross-expert quality variability observed in modern MoE models.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): calibration-free bit allocation for MoE quantization, needed because 'the original training data, and hence the true training distribution, is proprietary and inaccessible'. COMPRESSION RATIO: mixed precision across experts (no single ratio - that is the point of the method). QUALITY COST: no numeric delta in the abstract; recorded as a mechanism/diagnosis contribution.
